findings.text: settingsAllowIframe() runs repo.ServerSettings(context.Background()) on EVERY request (ignoring request context, error→false default) just to decide the CSP frame-ancestors header — direct documented ARCHITECTURE.md rule violation ('cache read-mostly settings and invalidate through the settings-changed event, not a query per request'); real per-request DB overhead.

Read-only Handler and Runtime both ship production implementations of /status, /ping, /healthcheck, unsupported() and auth (selected by cfg.ReadOnly) and disagree observably: read-only /status refuses authLoginCustomMessage with 501 while Runtime sanitizes it with auth.SanitizeHTML; read-only also accepts authActiveAuthMethods as []any OR []string while Runtime only []any. Same route, two behaviors by mode.

Restore concurrency hazard: Manager.ServeHTTP releases the mutex then calls rt.ServeHTTP, so in-flight requests keep executing against oldRuntime while restore runs oldRuntime.close(false) and oldStore.Close() concurrently — requests race teardown instead of getting the 503 'server is restarting'.

Dispatch uses 13 hand-rolled Handle(w, r, user) bool chains + string-prefix routes instead of the planned Phase-5 ServeMux strangler — documented ratchet-tracked legacy state; but /api/tasks is additionally special-cased inline in the dispatcher (390-398) despite audiotools.Handle being on the chain, an inconsistent one-off glue point.
backup.Options constructed twice in newRuntime with an identical repeated block (BACKUP_PATH env → settings backupPath, maxBackupSize default, manager wiring); should share one builder.

Log level derived by substring match anywhere in the message ('error'/'warn' inside ordinary text escalates level); entries are map[string]any; globally installs log.SetOutput once — benign but over-fit level inference.
Cosmetics: routePath's bool always true even when the base prefix doesn't match (dead ok() contract); `_ = claims` discards the authenticate() result it just returned.
newRuntime repeats the manual teardown triplet (podcastsHandler.Close(); hub.Close(); sc.Close()) three times down error paths instead of deferrable cleanup.
Manager restore happy-path and rollback well tested; RW Runtime dispatcher has only one request-level unit test — dispatch-order/auth-placement correctness relies on the external parity harness.
